extracted.intended_audience: attorneys admitted to practice before the USPTO, OED staff, state disciplinary agencies, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing reciprocal discipline on an attorney based on a state-bar suspension, specifying suspension length, reinstatement and probation procedures, notice/publication requirements, and related obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline trigger (37 C.F.R. § 11.24 / § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) based on having been suspended from the practice of law on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director filed a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting that the USPTO Director impose reciprocal discipline for such a state suspension. The Final Order cites the State Bar of Texas suspension as the triggering misconduct for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity to respond (Notice and Order / 40-day requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director issued a Notice and Order giving Respondent 40 days to file a response 'containing all information that Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact' that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail. If returned undelivered, the Notice may be published in the Official Gazette. Failure to file a timely response may result in a determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for imposing identical discipline (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the Director may impose discipline identical to that imposed by a State unless the respondent establishes a genuine issue of material fact warranting a different sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, Respondent did not file a response; the Office determined there was no genuine issue of material fact and accordingly imposed discipline identical in effect (suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension length and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the USPTO for ten (10) years, with two (2) years of active suspension and eight (8) years of probated suspension thereafter if the Respondent complies with the requirements set forth by the State Bar of Texas to receive probated suspension in that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension commences on the date of the Final Order; the probationary portion is contingent on satisfying state-imposed conditions for probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition timing and conditions (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is permitted to file a petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 at any time after two (2) years from the date the Final Order is signed; for any petition filed within the ten (10) year suspension period, Respondent must first have complied with the State Bar of Texas requirements to receive probated suspension in that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with state conditions is a precondition to filing for reinstatement within the suspension period; petitions are governed by § 11.60 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate reinstatement and stay of remaining suspension (OED Director authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's immediate reinstatement, the OED Director shall stay any remaining period of suspension and the Respondent will serve a period of probation during that remaining period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An OED-granted immediate reinstatement results in a stay of any remaining suspension and substitution of a probationary regime as defined by the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'remaining period of suspension'
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'remaining period of suspension' means (a) Respondent's initial 10 year suspension minus the period of time from the date the Final Order is signed until Respondent is reinstated; and (b) if Respondent has not been reinstated prior to 10 years from the date the Final Order is signed, there is no 'remaining period of suspension.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the mathematical/temporal rule for calculating any stayed portion of suspension if reinstatement occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation enforcement procedure (Order to Show Cause; 15-day response; referral)
rubrics_metrics.description: If during the probationary period the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent at the last address of record, and grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after the 15-day response period the OED Director still concludes there was noncompliance, the OED Director shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for the failure to comply. The steps and timelines are mandatory procedural protections before further discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of review on discipline (no automatic stay)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the USPTO Director enters an order disciplining Respondent and Respondent seeks review of such order, any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for review do not automatically stay the disciplinary action; discipline remains in effect while review is pending unless otherwise ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of suspension (Official Gazette notice content)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, the relevant rule violated (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), the period of suspension, reinstatement eligibility, and that Respondent is not authorized to practice before the Office in patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a model Notice of Suspension with factual background (state suspension date, basis for state suspension, specific disciplinary rule violations, description of misconduct) and provides a link to the OED Reading Room for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures inter-jurisdictional notification of the USPTO discipline and its grounds to relevant authorities and public bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Order does not restate § 11.58, this incorporates the statutory duties (e.g., obligations to notify clients, courts, and other duties prescribed by § 11.58) as conditions of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct leading to state suspension (basis for discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Bar of Texas found Respondent violated Texas Disciplinary Rules 1.14(a), 1.14(b), 1.15(d), and 8.04(a)(1) for agreeing to assist a client with a prior art search and file a patent application, accepting $10,250.00 for prepayment of expenses, failing to hold the funds separate from his own property, and failing to provide the client with an accounting or a copy of the client's file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual findings illustrate the sorts of professional misconduct (mishandling client funds, lack of accounting, failure to return client file) that can support reciprocal discipline before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citations for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations identify the statutory and regulatory bases that support the USPTO's authority to impose reciprocal discipline and to provide notice; useful guidance for procedural and jurisdictional authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catchall relief and continuing jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order provides for 'such other and further relief as the nature of this cause shall require.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a general reservation of authority to impose additional or ancillary relief as necessary to effectuate the disciplinary objectives.
